Dismiss Opt out Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information Governance 5 min read From red tape to right to business: Bihar unveils major reforms to attract investments, accelerate industrialisation Bihar’s new Ease of Doing Business framework promises faster approvals, self-certification and fewer inspections, aiming to attract investment, accelerate industrialisation and generate employment. Anoop Verma ETGovernment Updated On Oct 11, 2026 at 07:37 AM IST Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary Bihar’s Ease of Doing Business Act, 2026, introduces a major shift in industrial governance, allowing enterprises to begin operations through self-declaration, securing time-bound approvals and establishing a single authority responsible for investment clearances. The reforms could strengthen Bihar’s competitiveness as an industrial destination, provided implementation matches legislative ambition. Advt The state is attempting to dismantle one of the most persistent barriers to industrialisation in India: the complex regulatory system that forces entrepreneurs to navigate multiple departments, secure numerous permissions and endure uncertain approval timelines before establishing a business. Through three notifications issued on October 9, 2026, under the Bihar Ease of Doing Business Act, 2026, the state government has initiated a potentially significant transformation in its industrial governance framework. The legislation seeks to replace permission-based administration with a system founded on entrepreneurial freedom, regulatory accountability, self-certification and time-bound decision-making. ANI Updated On Oct 11, 2026 at 05:38 AM IST No decision taken yet on Maa Sita University; consultations to begin after MLC polls, says Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary Patna: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary instructed Higher Education Minister Sanjay Singh Tiger to take any decision regarding the proposed Maa Sita Women's University only after consulting the relevant stakeholders and taking their suggestions into account. Advt The Chief Minister clarified that consultations with stakeholders and further action will commence only after the ongoing Bihar Legislative Council election process concludes. He stated that a meeting must be convened with all stakeholders associated with the proposed university to review their suggestions and views. A final decision will subsequently be made based on the feedback received, with officials confirming that no final decision has been taken regarding the university as of now. bihar_raw_news.title: BIADA MD Naveen Kumar Inspects Patliputra Industrial Area In Bihar - Oneindia News
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar News: BIADA MD Inspects Patliputra Industrial Area, Directs Action Against Encroachments and Illegal Construction India -Oneindia Staff By Oneindia Staff Updated: Sunday, October 11, 2026, 10:39 [IST] Add as a preferred source on Google Patna, October 10, 2026: Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) Managing Director Naveen Kumar, IAS, inspected the Patliputra Industrial Area on Saturday and reviewed infrastructure facilities, data centre operations and the activities of various industrial units. During the visit, he directed officials to take time-bound action on issues related to encroachments, unauthorised construction, sanitation, traffic management and infrastructure maintenance. BIADA MD Inspects Patliputra Industrial Area AI Summary AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors BIADA Managing Director Naveen Kumar, IAS, inspected Patliputra Industrial Area to assess infrastructure, data centre operations, and facilities. He directed time-bound actions against encroachments, unauthorised construction, sanitation lapses, and parking issues, and ordered monitoring of construction compliance and road restoration to strengthen the investor-friendly environment in Bihar. Switch To Shorts The inspection focused on ensuring better management of the industrial area, maintaining cleanliness and enforcing applicable rules. The Managing Director also reviewed the condition of roads and other civic facilities and instructed officials to address the issues identified during the visit within the stipulated timeframe. During the inspection, Naveen Kumar visited several industrial and commercial establishments, including Ravi Industry, Recon Engicon Pvt. Ltd., UNO Digital Pvt. Ltd., SLMG Beverage Pvt. Ltd., Prius System LLP, CtrlS, Ambe Infra Green LLP, Aeron Healthcare Pvt. Ltd., Bihar Trade Tower, Vijayam Educational Trust, Maa Re Rolling Mill, Puja Printech Pvt. Ltd., Satya Enterprises, Eclet Industries Ltd., Civ Mill Industries Pvt. Ltd., Tirupati Industries and Ruby Fastner. He assessed various operational and infrastructure-related concerns and directed the concerned officials to ensure timely corrective action. Access Control System to Be Implemented at Entry Gates To regulate the movement of private vehicles within the industrial area, the BIADA Managing Director directed officials to implement an access control system at all entry gates. He also instructed officials to take immediate action, in accordance with applicable rules, against industrial units found storing construction materials without authorisation along the main roads and internal roads. Strict Action on Waste Dumping and Sanitation Issues Emphasising the need to maintain cleanliness, Kumar directed officials to ensure the immediate cleaning and removal of waste from the industrial area. He further instructed them to conduct awareness campaigns through public announcements and issue notices to industrial units to prevent waste dumping along roadsides. Violations will be dealt with in accordance with the applicable rules. The directions aim to improve sanitation and ensure that roads and public spaces within the industrial area remain clean and accessible. Action Against Unauthorised Parking and Construction on BIADA Land The Managing Director directed officials to take action under the applicable rules against unauthorised vehicle parking on BIADA land near the Polytechnic and Sai Temple. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate projects worth 13,000 crore rupees in Chennai, Tamil Nadu today. Prime Minister will flag off the metro rail service of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around 4900 crore rupees. Mr Modi will also undertake a ride on the Chennai Metro from Porur Bypass Station to Poonamallee Bypass Station and back. The Poonamallee – Porur corridor features a unique 3.7-km double-decker structure with advanced signalling systems designed to support driverless operations. The Prime Minister will dedicate and inaugurate railway infrastructure projects worth over 750 crore rupees, including five Amrit Stations at Palani, Vellore Cantonment, Ambasamudram, Paramakudi and Namakkal, which have been redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat Station scheme. Mr Modi will perform Darshan and Pooja at the Jalakandeswarar Temple near the Porur lake. The stage is all set for the Prime Minister’s visit today at Chennai. The city has brightened up to welcome the Prime Minister as he is set to launch several projects based on infrastructure in road development , ports and innovation in sciences. This includes laying the foundation stone and inauguration of key National Highway projects to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency. The road projects will reduce the travel time apart from easing traffic congestion in National Highways in Salem, Madurai and Nagapattinam. He will also lay the foundation stone for Lube Oil Base Stocks project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited. The prime minister will also inaugurate an additional Coal Berth project and lay the foundation stone for capital dredging works for additional Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port . Mr Modi will dedicate to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras, a pioneering global scientific mission to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, across the human lifespan – from the foetal stage to old age. Prime Minister will participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya School in Chennai before leaving to Delhi.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 37 Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana completes one year today
national_raw_news.content: Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana has completed one year today. The scheme was launched on this day last year to strengthen agriculture in 100 Aspirational Agricultural Districts across the country. Our correspondent reports that the scheme has brought together 36 Central schemes across 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private sector participation, to address district-specific agricultural needs. India’s agriculture sector has significant potential across diverse regions and farming communities. Approved by the Union Cabinet in July last year, the six-year initiative was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 11th October last year. It brings together 36 Central schemes across 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private sector participation, to address district-specific agricultural needs. PMDDKY completed its first year, today marking a year of focused district-level action. Across 100 districts, District Action Plans and indicator-based monitoring are now in place. District-specific interventions are supporting agricultural development on the ground. The scheme aims to improve agricultural productivity, irrigation facilities, access to credit and post-harvest infrastructure. The Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana follows a three-tier implementation structure at the district, state and national levels. District Action Plans are prepared according to local agricultural needs, with progress monitored through one hundred twenty one indicators across 36 Central schemes. During the first year, all 100 selected districts prepared their action plans, which are under implementation. The average performance score of these districts increased from 18.85 in April 2026 to 46.89 in August 2026, reflecting improvement across all six objectives of the scheme. The initiative has also promoted knowledge-sharing among farmers. The PM-DDKY Farmer Producer Organisations Sangam, held in December 2025, brought together more than 72 Farmer Producer Organisations from 15 States and 33 scheme districts to share experiences and explore opportunities in agricultural productivity, market access and income enhancement. The progress achieved provides a foundation for stronger convergence and sustained agricultural development in the years ahead.
